newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms new president faces challenge.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms new president faces challenge.

text.p: The newly named president of Tele-Communications Inc, Leo Hindery, comes on board at a challenging time for the giant cable operator, analysts said.
The Englewood, Colorado-based company, has disappointed its investors and angered customers with rate hikes and channel lines up changes that have turned into public relations nightmares.
"Customer perception, customer focus, customer service -- all need dramatic improvement," said James Jungjohann of A. G. Edwards.
Jungjohann added that Wall Street investors are also looking for improvement in the price of the stock.
Shares on Friday rose 1/8 to 13-7/8, but are still lingering too close to the 52-week low of 11-5/16.
In December TCI announced a cost-cutting program that included layoffs of 2,500 employees, or about 6.5 percent of its workforce, salary cuts and freezes for executives.
Hindery has been managing general partner and chief executive of InterMedia Partners, a San Francisco-based cable operator that is partly owned by TCI.

That relationship is important, said Sharon Armbrust, senior analyst with Paul Kagan. "He's already very much on the same wavelength as John Malone," she said. Company chairman Malone relinquished the president's post earlier Friday.
She said the other talent Hindery brings to the table is his reputation as a "no nonsense" manager with good operating skills.
"Malone is the strategist and Hindery will be the implementer," Armbrust said.
In its announcement, TCI said the CEO's of each of TCI's business units, communications, programming, international and techynology, will report to Hindery.
Armbrust said that is important because Malone's message and strategies will be delivered to its operating managers by a single voice.
